name: Mongolia: Ulaanbaatar, the Gobi and the Orkhon valley

cities.name: Gobi Gurvansaikhan: Yolyn Am and Bayanzag

cities.base: The row of camps along the Khongoryn Gol at the north foot of the dunes, about 2 km back from the sand. Simple gers, shared shower blocks, generator power until roughly 23:00, and a season of mid May
cities.name: The Khongoryn Els dunes

cities.name: Kharkhorin and the Orkhon valley

cities.name: Khovsgol: Hatgal and the west shore

cities.base: A camp in the main Terelj valley past Turtle Rock, 70 km and about 90 minutes from Ulaanbaatar on tarmac the whole way. This is the one base you can reach on a half day, which is why it works as the l
cities.name: Gorkhi-Terelj

places.name: Sukhbaatar Square
places.note: A parade ground with Chinggis on a throne at the north end and the Parliament behind him, and it is the one point in the city every other address is measured from.

places.name: National Museum of Mongolia
places.note: Three floors that run from deer stones to the 1990 democracy protests, and the upstairs hall of ethnic costume is the part that makes the countryside legible.

places.name: Chinggis Khaan National Museum
places.note: Opened in 2022, eight floors, and the lighting and object mounts are better than anything else in the country, though the empire floors lean hard on replicas and screens.

places.name: Gandantegchinlen Monastery
places.note: Come before 09:30 for the chanting in the smaller temples, then the 26 metre Migjid Janraisig statue, which is a 1996 replacement for the one the Soviets melted down.

places.name: Choijin Lama Temple Museum
places.note: Five temples from 1908 left standing as a museum instead of being demolished, and the tsam dance masks inside are the best religious objects in the city after the Zanabazar.

places.name: Zanabazar Museum of Fine Arts
places.note: Small and badly lit, but the gilt bronze Tara and Vajradhara that Zanabazar cast in the 1680s are the finest objects made in Mongolia and they are in room one.

places.name: Bogd Khan Winter Palace Museum
places.note: The last Bogd Khan lived here until 1924 and the collection is his actual stuff, including a ger lined with the skins of 150 snow leopards, which is uncomfortable and worth seeing.

places.name: Narantuul Market
places.note: Locals call it the Black Market and it is mostly Chinese clothing, plus a saddle and deel row at the back; pickpocketing is constant and the payoff is thin, so buy your cashmere at the State Department Store instead.

places.name: Tumen Ekh Ensemble
places.note: An hour of khoomei throat singing, morin khuur and a contortionist, aimed squarely at tourists but the musicians are genuinely good and it runs nightly in summer.

places.name: Modern Nomads 2
places.note: Mongolian food done properly indoors: buuz, khuushuur, boodog and a mutton soup that tastes like the countryside version without the grit.

places.name: Rosewood Kitchen and Enoteca
places.note: The one place in Ulaanbaatar where the cooking and the wine list are both serious, which matters more than it sounds after four nights of camp mutton.

places.name: Millie's Espresso
places.note: Expat canteen since the 1990s, real espresso and a decent breakfast, and the noticeboard is still where drivers and guides get found.

places.name: Yolyn Am
places.note: A narrowing limestone gorge in the Zuunmod valley where a sheet of river ice survives into July in cold years; the walk in is 4 km, flat, and the ice is often gone by early August.

places.name: Gurvan Saikhan Nature Museum
places.note: A single room of stuffed argali, lammergeier and a few dinosaur bones at the valley entrance, worth the fifteen minutes because it names what you are about to fail to spot.

places.name: Dungenee Canyon
places.note: The next gorge west of Yolyn Am and almost empty by comparison, with the same walls and no ice, so go here if the Yolyn Am car park has six minivans in it.

places.name: Mukhar Shivert Gorge
places.note: A short side canyon with a seasonal ice shelf and a scramble at the head; drivers use it as the wet weather substitute for Yolyn Am.

places.name: Bayanzag, the Flaming Cliffs
places.note: Roy Chapman Andrews found the first known dinosaur eggs in these red beds in 1922; the cliffs are only about 40 metres high and look ordinary at noon, so time it for the last hour of light.

places.name: Moltsog Els
places.note: A low dune field ten minutes from the Flaming Cliffs that most itineraries pair with them, useful as a warm up if you are not going on to Khongoryn Els.

places.name: Khavtsgait Petroglyphs
places.note: Bronze Age rock carvings of ibex, carts and hunters scattered over a boulder ridge; the climb is 30 minutes of loose scree and nobody marks which rocks have the good panels, so take the camp guide.

places.name: Three Camel Lodge
places.note: The one Gobi camp built to lodge standards, with proper bathrooms in the gers and a real kitchen; it is roughly triple the price of a standard camp and books out months ahead in July.

places.name: Sundowner on the Bayanzag rim
places.note: Camps will send you out with a thermos or a bottle for the hour before sunset, which is the only time the red actually does what the photographs claim.

places.name: South Gobi Provincial Museum
places.note: Provincial museum with fossil casts and local Buddhist objects, useful only as a way to fill the gap between landing at Dalanzadgad and the camp being ready.

places.name: Dalanzadgad Market
places.note: Concrete hall and a yard of container shops; this is the last place to buy water, batteries and a warm layer before four days where the nearest shop is 150 km away.

places.name: The Khongoryn Els dune climb
places.note: The high ridge is about 250 metres of pure sand and the climb takes 45 to 70 minutes of one step back for two forward; go at 07:00 before the sand gets too hot to sit on.

places.name: Sunset on the Khongoryn ridge
places.note: You do not have to summit for this; the lower shoulder at the north end catches the same light and the sand hums audibly when it slides.

places.name: The Khongoryn Gol oasis
places.note: A green ribbon of reeds and poplars running along the base of the dunes with herder gers and horses in it, and the contrast with the sand two hundred metres away is the actual picture.

places.name: Bactrian camel ride at the dune foot
places.note: Ninety minutes on a two humped camel led by the herder family who own them; it is slow and genuinely uncomfortable after forty minutes, and it is still the thing people remember.

places.name: Khorkhog dinner at the camp
places.note: Mutton cooked in a milk churn with fire heated river stones, ordered a day ahead for the whole camp; the stones come round afterwards and you are meant to hold them.

places.name: The Sevrei Uul road
places.note: The track south of the dunes climbs over the Sevrei range and gives you the only place from which the whole 100 km dune chain lines up at once.
places.neighborhood: Sevrei range, south of the dunes

places.name: Sevrei soum village
places.note: Two hundred people, a school, a fuel pump and a new white stupa, and stopping here for twenty minutes tells you more about how the Gobi actually works than the dunes do.

places.name: The Gobi night sky from camp
places.note: There is no artificial light for 150 km and the camp generator normally cuts at 23:00, which is when it gets good; bring a down layer, it drops near freezing even in July.

places.name: Airag and aaruul at a herder ger
places.note: Fermented mare's milk, dried curd and snuff passed the correct way round; it is arranged by your driver and the airag is genuinely sour, so take the smallest sip you can manage politely.

places.name: Khermen Tsav
places.note: A red canyon system and one of the great dinosaur beds, but it is five hours of unmarked track each way from the dunes and there is nowhere to sleep; on a 12 day trip it costs you the Orkhon valley.

places.name: Erdene Zuu Monastery
places.note: Founded in 1585 out of the stone of Karakorum, walled by 108 stupas, and reduced from over sixty temples to three in the 1937 purge; the three that survive hold the good sculpture.

places.name: Kharkhorin Museum
places.note: Built with Japanese money in 2011 and the only place that makes the Karakorum site comprehensible, because the city itself is a grass field with nothing standing.

places.name: The Karakorum stone turtle
places.note: One of four granite turtles that marked the corners of Ogedei's capital, now alone in a field of weeds, and it is close to all that is left above ground of the Mongol imperial city.

places.name: The Kharkhorin phallic rock
places.note: A carved stone penis pointed at a hillside cleft, sold hard by every driver as a stop; it is twenty minutes of your day for a joke you can see in one photograph.

places.name: Khar Balgas
places.note: The earth walls of Ordu-Baliq, the Uighur capital of 751, still standing several metres high over a square kilometre; there are no signs, no fence and usually nobody else.

places.name: Khoshoo Tsaidam and the Orkhon inscriptions
places.note: The Bilge Khagan and Kul Tegin stelae of 732 and 735, the oldest writing in a Turkic language, housed in a small museum built by Turkey; the original site mounds are in the field outside.

places.name: Tuvkhun Monastery
places.note: Zanabazar's retreat at 2300 metres, reached by three hours of rough track from Kharkhorin plus a 40 minute climb through larch; the track is impassable after heavy rain and drivers will turn back.

places.name: Orkhon waterfall, Ulaan Tsutgalan
places.note: Twenty metres of water over a basalt lip into a 22 metre gorge, four to five hours of rocky track each way from Kharkhorin, and it barely runs until the first real summer rains in late July.

places.name: Shankh Monastery
places.note: Founded 1647, held Chinggis Khaan's black war banner for a time, kept alive underground through the purge years by monks who buried the texts; twenty or so monks are back.

places.name: Elsen Tasarkhai
places.note: An 80 km strip of sand dunes sitting in grassland on the paved road between Ulaanbaatar and Kharkhorin, camel rides and all; a fair leg stretch, not a substitute for Khongoryn Els.

places.name: Khustain Nuruu National Park
places.note: The takhi, the only never domesticated horse left, reintroduced here from zoos in 1992 and now several hundred; they come down to the valleys at dusk and dawn and you will see them from a vehicle at distance.
places.neighborhood: Altanbulag sum, 100 km west of Ulaanbaatar

places.name: Uushigiin Uvur deer stones
places.note: Fourteen Bronze Age stelae carved with flying stags, about 3000 years old, standing in an open field with a khirigsuur burial mound behind them; this is the best deer stone site in the country and it is on the way from the airport.

places.name: Murun Market
places.note: Provincial market where the Darkhad and Tsaatan families buy flour and rope; last real supermarket before the lake, and the only place to get cash that reliably works.

places.name: Hatgal village
places.note: A former Soviet port of wooden houses and a rusting fleet at the lake's south end, now mostly guesthouses and horse touts; scruffy, and the working end of the whole region.

places.name: Buuz at a Hatgal guanz
places.note: Canteen mutton dumplings, tsuivan and salty milk tea for a few dollars; the menu is whatever the board says and there will not be a vegetable in it.

places.name: The Jankhai pass
places.note: The track up the west shore climbs a low saddle about 25 km north of Hatgal and this is the first point the lake reads as an inland sea rather than a bay.

places.name: The Khovsgol lake boat
places.note: Private launches run three hour trips from Hatgal towards Modon Khuis island; boats only sail mid June to early September and a north wind cancels them without much warning.

places.name: West shore horse trek
places.note: Five hours on a Mongolian horse along the shore and up into the larch; the saddles are wooden, there are no helmets unless you bring one, and the horses respond to chu and nothing else.

places.name: Swimming off the west shore
places.note: The lake holds one percent of the world's fresh water and sits around 10 to 12 degrees in August, so this is a thirty second swim and a long sit on a hot rock afterwards.

places.name: A Tsaatan reindeer camp visit
places.note: Two or three families bring reindeer near the lake in summer for visitors, which is a staged version; the real taiga camps are two days of riding north from Tsagaannuur and need their own week.
places.neighborhood: West shore or Ulaan Uul road

places.name: Khankh, the north end
places.note: The Russian border village at the top of the lake, reached by a rough five hour drive up the east shore or a long boat; on a 12 day trip it eats two days for scenery you already have.

places.name: Melkhii Khad, Turtle Rock
places.note: A 24 metre granite tor that does look like a turtle, surrounded by souvenir stalls and camel touts; five minutes of looking, then walk 300 metres away and the crowd is gone.

places.name: Aryabal Meditation Temple
places.note: 108 steps up a wooden staircase to a small temple shaped like an elephant's head, with Buddhist proverbs on boards the whole way up; the view back down the valley is the reason to climb it.

places.name: The Chinggis Khaan Equestrian Statue at Tsonjin Boldog
places.note: Forty metres of stainless steel on a plinth, built in 2008, with a lift to a viewing platform on the horse's head; the museum underneath is thin and the whole stop is a photograph plus a car park.

places.name: The Secret History of the Mongols monument
places.note: A low stone wall carved with passages from the 13th century Secret History, standing beside the statue car park and ignored by everyone heading for the lift.

places.name: The Terelj river valley walk
places.note: Two hours along the Terelj river between granite towers and larch, starting from any camp in the main valley; flat, unmarked, and the best cheap hour of the whole trip.

places.name: Khagiin Khar lake
places.note: A glacial lake 60 km up the valley at the head of the park, reached on horseback over two days or by a rough three hour drive when the river crossings are low.

places.name: Gunjiin Sum
places.note: A 1740 Manchu temple left as one roofless hall in the forest, 30 km north of the camps on a track that needs a river crossing; go for the ride in rather than the ruin.

places.name: Terelj horse ride
places.note: Two hours out of the camp herd, arranged the night before; these are the most ridden horses in Mongolia and correspondingly the calmest, which is the right place to learn.

places.name: Ger camp dinner in Terelj
places.note: Set menu at a fixed hour, usually soup then mutton then tinned fruit, eaten in a big communal ger; ask in the morning if you want the vegetarian version and they will manage it.

places.name: Camp bar and the fire
places.note: Chinggis vodka, Sengur beer and a stove that someone comes to light at 22:00 and again at 05:00; that second visit is the reason you sleep through a two degree night.

places.name: The Gorkhi-Terelj park gate
places.note: Where the fee is collected and the tarmac gives out; from here the valley narrows fast and the day trip buses turn round within ten kilometres.

outings.why: Sukhbaatar Square, the National Museum and the Chinggis Khaan National Museum are within four hundred metres of each other, so this is the one genuinely walkable half day of the trip. Both museums are big; do not try to add Gandan to the sa
outings.name: The Ulaanbaatar museum morning
outings.season: All year. Both run daily 15 May to 14 September and drop a c
outings.fallback: The National Museum alone, two hours, then lunch.

outings.why: The religious and art half of the city, spread over about 3 km, so one short taxi hop in the middle. Gandan wants to be first for the morning chanting. Choijin Lama shuts Sundays and Mondays in winter.
outings.name: Gandan, Choijin Lama and the Zanabazar
outings.fallback: Gandan plus the Modern Art Gallery if the Zanabazar is between hangs.

outings.why: Wrestling and the opening ceremony in the stadium on 11 July, the archery field next door, and then 40 km west to the horse racing on the steppe, which is where the real event happens. Stadium tickets sell out months ahead and the road out
outings.name: Naadam at the National Sports Stadium and Khui Doloon Khudag
outings.season: 11 to 13 July, every year. 2027 falls 11 to 15 July.
outings.fallback: Skip the stadium, drive out to Khui Doloon Khudag for the horse finish only, and be back by 15:00.

outings.why: Drive an hour into the Zuunmod valley, walk 4 km up a narrowing limestone gorge that holds river ice into July, and walk back. Flat, easy, and you can ride a pony the first kilometre. The ice is the point and it is usually gone by early Aug
outings.name: Yolyn Am
outings.season: Mid May to late September. Ice most reliable mid June to mid
outings.fallback: Dungenee canyon, thirty minutes away and almost empty.

outings.name: The Yolyn Am to Khongoryn Els drive
outings.season: Mid May to late September. Rain turns the last 40 km of sand
outings.fallback: None. There is no other road.

startsFrom.name: Gurvan Saikhan ger camps, west of Dalanzadgad

outings.why: The 250 metre climb to the high ridge at 07:00, roughly an hour up on sand that gives way under every step, twenty minutes on top and ten minutes sliding down. Then the camel string along the Khongoryn Gol in the late afternoon. The hardest
outings.name: The Khongoryn Els dunes
outings.season: Mid May to mid September. July afternoons hit 38C, so this i
outings.fallback: Walk the oasis poplars along the river and take the sunset shoulder at the north end instead of the summit.

startsFrom.name: Khongoryn Els camp row, Sevrei sum

outings.why: The Roy Chapman Andrews dinosaur beds, plus the Moltsog dune field and the Khavtsgait petroglyph ridge nearby. The cliffs themselves are 40 metres of red sandstone and they are flat and dull at midday, so this only works as a late afternoon
outings.name: Bayanzag and the Flaming Cliffs
outings.fallback: Cliffs and Moltsog only, skip the petroglyph scramble if it is over 35C.

outings.why: 380 km, mostly paved, six to eight hours in reality once you add the Khustai detour for the takhi wild horses and a lunch stop at Elsen Tasarkhai. Leave at 07:00 or you arrive at Erdene Zuu after it closes.
outings.name: The Ulaanbaatar to Kharkhorin drive with Khustain Nuruu
outings.season: May to October. Winter the same road takes ten hours.
outings.fallback: Straight through on the paved road, arrive Kharkhorin by 14:00, do Erdene Zuu the same afternoon.

outings.why: The 1585 monastery inside its wall of 108 stupas, then the Kharkhorin Museum, then ten minutes to the stone turtle standing alone in the grass where Ogedei's capital used to be. All on foot or a two minute drive between.
outings.name: Erdene Zuu and the Karakorum field
outings.season: All year, though the temples are unheated.
outings.fallback: Erdene Zuu and the museum, drop the turtle.

startsFrom.name: Kharkhorin ger camps, Orkhon river flats

outings.why: Three hours of rough track south from Kharkhorin into the Khangai, then a 40 minute climb through larch to Zanabazar's hermitage at 2300 metres, then the same back. Vehicles turn back after heavy rain and the last kilometre is walking whate
outings.name: Tuvkhun monastery
outings.season: June to late September. The track is closed by snow from Oct
outings.fallback: Shankh monastery, 30 km from Kharkhorin on a decent road, for the same idea in an hour.

startsFrom.name: Kharkhorin ger camps, Orkhon river flats

outings.why: Four to five hours each way from Kharkhorin on rocky river track for twenty metres of water. Worth it only if you sleep at a camp near the falls and pair it with Tuvkhun on the way, and only after late July when the rains have actually arri
outings.name: Orkhon waterfall, Ulaan Tsutgalan
outings.season: Late July to early September for water. Dry or a trickle bef
outings.fallback: Khar Balgas and the Khoshoo Tsaidam stelae, a six hour loop north up the valley on easier ground.

startsFrom.name: Kharkhorin ger camps, Orkhon river flats

outings.why: Land at Murun, drive 20 km west to the best deer stone field in Mongolia, then 100 km north to the lake on a road that is now mostly paved and takes two and a half hours. Do the stones on the way in, not as a separate trip.
outings.name: The Uushigiin Uvur deer stones and the road to Hatgal
outings.season: June to September, tied to the Murun flight window.
outings.fallback: Deer stones and straight to Hatgal, skip the Jankhai pass stop until the next day.

outings.why: Five hours in a wooden saddle up the shore and into the larch above Toilogt, with a herder leading. No helmets unless you bring your own, no stirrups you will like, and the horses only answer to chu.
outings.name: The Khovsgol west shore horse trek
outings.fallback: A two hour ride to the Jankhai pass and back, or the three hour boat from Hatgal.

startsFrom.name: West shore camps, Jankhai and Toilogt bays

outings.why: Three hours out of Hatgal towards Modon Khuis island on a private launch, which is the only way to understand the scale of a lake 136 km long. A north wind cancels it with about an hour of notice.
outings.name: The Khovsgol lake boat
outings.season: Mid June to early September, open water only.
outings.fallback: Drive the west shore track to Jankhai and walk the shingle.

startsFrom.name: West shore camps, Jankhai and Toilogt bays

outings.why: The granite tor, then the 108 steps up to the elephant head temple, then two hours along the Terelj river. Short, easy, and the one day on this trip that does not start with a drive.
outings.name: Turtle Rock and Aryabal
outings.season: May to early October. The steps ice over from November.
outings.fallback: The river valley walk alone, two hours from any camp door.

outings.why: Thirty kilometres north out of the Terelj camps to a roofless 1740 Manchu temple in the forest, on horseback or by vehicle with a river crossing. The ruin is modest; the ride through empty larch valleys is the actual day.

outings.season: June to September. The river crossing is impassable after he
outings.fallback: Khagiin Khar lake road as far as the vehicles can get, then turn round.

destination.name: Mongolia: Ulaanbaatar, the Gobi and the Orkhon valley
destination.pitch: Twelve days is enough for the capital, the Gobi and one northern valley, but only if you fly the long legs and accept that three of your days are spent inside a Land Cruiser.
destination.caveat: The whole country is open for about ninety days a year and the distances inside it are brutal, so a 12 day trip that tries to add Khovsgol to the Gobi and the Orkhon valley spends three full days driving and two more on domestic flights. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Ulaanbaatar is a Soviet grid with bad traffic, good museums and about four restaurants worth the trip. Two days, not four.
because.food: Weak and you should plan for it. Mutton, flour and dairy in three arrangements, and outside Ulaanbaatar a vegetable is a negotiation.
because.nature: Sand dunes 250 metres high, a limestone gorge that holds ice in July, and a lake holding one percent of the world's fresh water, with no fences or villages between any of them.
because.culture: Erdene Zuu, Zanabazar's bronzes, the 732 Orkhon inscriptions and the Uushigiin Uvur deer stones give you three thousand years in one valley system, and Naadam in July is a real festival rather than a performance.
because.adventure: Wooden saddles, no helmets, river crossings, a 250 metre sand climb and camps where the generator stops at 23:00.
because.relaxation: Low. Ger camps are quiet and the stove gets lit at 05:00, but the days either side are six hours of washboard track.
because.exploration: Outside Ulaanbaatar there are almost no signs, no marked trails and often no road, and your driver navigates by ridgelines, which is either the appeal or the problem.
